Each Plant shall have GNCPC of 1800(±5%) MW net on natural gas and when operated on back-up fuel the net power output shall follow Appendix C in the EPC Contract.  The Plant shall comprise of Power Blocks consisting of Gas turbines, HRSGs and Steam turbine. The additional power capacity achieved by SF must not exceed 10% of the Contracted Capacity.
Refer to section3 and 4 of OTS Part A.

itb.keywords: Combined Cycle Power Plant, dual fuel gas turbines (GTs), dry low NOx combustors, heat recovery steam generators (HRSGs), by-pass stack, diverter dampers, horizontal and vertical sealing guillotine damper, condensing steam turbine (CST), air cooled condenser, synchronous generators, generator circuit breakers (GTGs, STGs), generator step-up transformers (2 winding), auxiliary transformers (2 or 3 winding), HV circuit breakers for GSU transformers, symmetrical plant design, equally designed groups (GT/HRSG/ST)
itb.chunk_text:
The Plant shall be designed as a Combined Cycle Power Plant, consisting of but not limited to:
- Dual Fuel Gas Turbine (GTs)
- Dry low NOx combustors;
- Heat Recovery Steam Generators (HRSGs),
- By-pass  stack  including  diverter  dampers  horizontal  and  vertical  sealing  guillotine damper.
- Condensing Steam Turbine (CST) with Air Cooled Condenser
- Synchronous Generators for Gas Turbines and Steam Turbine
- Generator Circuit Breakers for GTGs and STGs
- 2 winding Generator Step-up transformers;
- 2 or 3 winding Auxiliary transformers
- HV Circuit Breakers for GSU Transformers of GTGs and STG
The plant shall be designed preferably symmetrically; this means the Plant shall consist of equally designed Groups (same number and type of GTs/HRSGs/ST).

itb.keywords: LP turbine exhaust to condenser transition, steam turbine outlet connection pieces, negligible pressure drop, turbine bypass dumps, dispersion headers internal to condenser, ACC materials selection, demineralized water chemistry, OEM guidelines, vacuum raising and maintaining plant, steam ejectors, mechanical vacuum pumps, hogging duty and running duty device (1+1 per condenser), HEI standards hotwell tank and condensate system, air ejector steam from main steam supply, ejector outlet silencer, condensate system instrumentation for condenser tube leakage
itb.chunk_text:
The steam turbine outlet connection pieces shall be designed for smooth transition with minimal obstructions from the LP turbine exhaust to the condenser to assure negligible pressure drop.
The turbine bypass dumps shall be designed with dispersion headers internal to the condenser to adequately disperse the steam safely into the condenser for all possible extreme transient scenarios.
The Air-Cooled condenser materials shall be selected to provide the necessary reliability at an economical cost taking into account that ACC is being operated with Demineralized water with proper water chemistry required by OEM guidelines. ACC OEM Design will take into consideration of proper material selection as per Demin water quality..
Vacuum raising and maintaining plant may be based on either steam ejectors or mechanical vacuum pumps. As a minimum, one start-up (hogging) duty and one running duty device shall be provided for each condenser.
Steam for air ejectors, if supplied, shall be taken from the main steam supply. A silencer shall be provided on each ejector outlet.
The hotwell tank and condensate system shall be sized in accordance with HEI standards.
The condensate system shall be equipped with instrumentation that will assist in trouble shooting of any condenser tube leakage.

itb.chunk_text:

The EPC Contractor shall supply all civil works required for gas station according to the requirements for Rumah and Nairyah. The design for the gas installations shall be carried out in close coordination with SPPC and Saudi Aramco

itb.chunk_text:
The EPC Contractor shall connect the Back-up Fuel system of the respective plant of Rumah or Nairyah IPPs or both to the Back-up Fuel tank farm.
Each of the Back-up Fuel oil tanks shall be placed on reinforced concrete ring foundations and be located inside an oil and watertight tank basin of reinforced concrete slabs and surrounding walls with respective oil proof coating.
In addition, the EPC Contractor shall supply all civil works required for Back-up Fuel delivery by road tankers through an unloading station located adjacent to the Back-up Fuel storage tanks within the plant boundaries.

itb.chunk_text:
The HRSG shall be designed and sized based on the Design Point Performance (to be chosen at a later stage) operating on natural gas specified on OTS Part A Annex 4.1-1 Fuel Gas Specification.
The  HRSG  shall  be  equipped  with  cold  end  condensate  recirculation  system  and  condensate  bypass arrangement. The HRSG shall achieve the desired plant performance at all the operating points.
In  case  of  cold  casing  design,  the  HRSG  design  shall  incorporate  adequate  hot  &  cold  end  corrosion protections. Hot and Cold end corrosion protective measures shall include Protective coatings on the casing and protective layers (Teflon or other suitable corrosion protection layers) to minimise the undesirable effects of sulphuric acid corrosion. Alternatively, hot casing design for HRSG shall be provided for hot and cold  end  corrosion  protection.  The  corrosion  protection  methods  employed  shall  be  having  proven commercial operational experience and shall be approved by the OWNER.
To satisfy the operational requirement as mentioned in OTS Part A. In order to model the degradation due to aging, the following information shall be supplied for HRSG for years following post COD starting from guaranteed values, but applying best estimate degradation in addition to submitting the long-term best estimate degradation curve or factors:
- Enthalpy of the exhaust gas
- Mass flow of the exhaust gas
- Temperature of the exhaust gas
- Exhaust Gas composition
- The pressure, temperature and steam flow of each pressure level
HP steam, after expansion in the HP ST, can be equally split over 2 or 3 HRSGs for reheating, without creating unbalances in the respective HRSGs (if reheat system is applied).
Condensate return temperature shall be above dew point temperature, to minimize corrosion risk.

itb.keywords: applicable environmental laws and standards, permits for plant construction, Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA), Preliminary Environmental Assessment (PEA), Environmental and Social Impact Assessment (ESIA), international lenders requirements, Equator Principles III (2013), IFC Performance Standards (2012), Environmental Permit, Waste Management Plan (construction), Hazardous Area Classification drawings, ANSI/API RP-505, Company Standard SAES-B-068, hazardous locations classification, plot plans, process schedule of hazardous materials, ventilation system failure, area classification documentation, equipment uniquely identified in classified areas
itb.chunk_text:
The  Contractor  will  be  required  to  design  and  construct  the  Plant  in  accordance  with  the  applicable environmental laws and standards. The Contractor is also responsible for obtaining and maintaining all the necessary Permits for the construction of the Plant.
An Environmental Impact Assessment Study (EIA) will be completed by Owner and copy of the same will be made available to Contractor. A Preliminary Environmental Assessment ('PEA') or Environmental and Social Impact Assessment ('E S IA') was conducted by the Offtaker and is provided in OTS Part A, Annex 3.31 of Part III (Drawings and Diagrams).
It is anticipated that the Project's development will necessitate the involvement of international lenders for financing. Given this, the Project's assessment will need to account for the requirements of international lenders in addition to the local regulations. With the specific international lenders currently unknown, the key requirements, which have been considered within this Scoping report, comprise the Equator Principles III (2013) and associated IFC Performance Standards (2012). The Project will be expected to comply with the most stringent standards should national/IFC requirements differ.
The Owner will progress the EIA Study with the intention that the Environmental Permit is available soon after the time of Contract Award. Contractor shall be responsible for providing all the necessary technical and environmental inputs to the extent required for the EIA study. After Contract Award any amendment to  the  EIA  Study  and  the  Environmental  Permit  will  be  the  responsibility  of  the  Owner  and  the  EPC Contractor.
Waste management during construction will be in accordance with the Waste Management Plan developed specifically for this project and in accordance with Government and Company approved plan.
Hazardous  Area  Classification  drawings  shall  be  developed  in  accordance  with  the  latest  revision  of ANSI/API  RP-505  and  Company  Standard  SAES-B-068  during  the  PP  Phase.  The  Area  Classification drawings shall be prepared from the project plot plans and the process schedule of hazardous materials to determine the potential sources of hazard.
All areas of the where concentrations of gas may occur due to normal leakage or process fault or ventilation system failure shall be classed as hazardous locations. The Contractor shall calculate and produce area classification drawings and documentation for the whole site area. The classified area shall be as defined within the relevant regulations and standards. All equipment within each area shall be uniquely identified and be fully compliant with the standards and regulations.

itb.chunk_text:
- 1) NOX emission for Back-up Fuel is based on maximum fuel bound nitrogen content of 0.015% by weight.
- 2) This value of 18 mg/Nm3 (or 9 ppmv) applies for combined cycle operation.
- 3) In case open cycle is implemented, this value may be exceeded up to a value of maximum 50 mg/Nm3 subject to the approval by the competent authorities
- 4) In case open cycle is implemented, this value may be exceeded up to a value of maximum 150 mg/Nm3 subject to the approval by the competent authorities
Emission guarantees are given for a daily average and for steady state operation and normal loading and deloading transients. Emissions guarantees will not apply to grid code compliance or frequency following transients.
The values in above table refer to the flue (exhaust) gas in dry condition, 0 °C temperature and 1013 mbar atmospheric pressure.
Emissions control system to meet the requirements of IFC guidelines, World Bank, Equator Principles III (2013) and Royal Commission requirements.
The gaseous emissions from the plant shall not exceed the limits as specified in the above guidelines and as per Environmental and Social Impact Assessment (ESIA) study report.
The emission guarantee of gas turbine is suggested for purpose of SCR design:
- <Natural Gas firing>
- -Ambient temperature is more than 15 degC: from 60% to 100 of the gas turbine load.
- -Ambient temperature is less than 15 degC: from 80% to 100 of the gas turbine load.
- <Back up Fuel firing>
-Ambient temperature is more than 15 degC: from 60% to 100 of the gas turbine load.
-Ambient temperature is less than 15 degC: from 75% to 100 of the gas turbine load.

itb.keywords: undue vibration, least practicable noise, noise standards and guidelines, OTS Part A Section 4.1.9.5, noise levels measured according to ISO standards, noise attenuation features, permissible noise limits, silencers, lagging, acoustic enclosures
itb.chunk_text:
All plant shall run without undue vibration and with the least practicable amount of noise.
The Plant shall be designed to achieve all the relevant noise standards and guidelines. As a minimum the Plant shall be designed to meet the requirements as per OTS part A section 4.1.9.5.
The noise levels shall be measured according to ISO standards.
To meet the noise level requirements the Plant is required to be equipped with standard noise attenuation features. All machinery which exceeds the permissible noise limits shall be equipped with silencers or with lagging or specially designed acoustic enclosures.

itb.keywords: sewage treatment plant, domestic and sanitary wastewater, industrial wastewater treated separately, wastewater collection and segregation, backwash water, rinse water, chemical and acid cleaning wastes, blow-down water, sewers or pipes (customary proven materials), pumping stations (geodetic constraints), cesspools intermediate storage, oil separators (oil contaminated water)
itb.chunk_text:
The sewage treatment plant and its ancillary systems shall fulfil the requirements to collect, treat/clarify and discharge the domestic and sanitary waste waters streams. The industrial wastewater shall be treated separately in adequate system. Both, domestic and industrial wastes consist of many compounds which could contaminate surface water) groundwater and soil. Furthermore, especially in the case of discharging untreated sanitary wastewater, the bacteriological contamination can result in the occurrence and spread of water borne diseases like cholera, dysentery, typhoid, etc. Therefore, special attention has to be paid by the Contractor during its investigation of the wastewater collection area to ensure that all waste water streams are considered and will be segregated, collected and discharged in a wastewater collecting system. This also includes all the sanitary and other domestic wastewater out of all permanent and temporary site facilities and the industrial wastewater out of the process like backwash water, rinse water, chemical and acid cleaning wastes and other process wastewater which cannot be used in other ways (blow-down water, etc.).
The wastewater shall be delivered to the wastewater treatment plant in sewers or pipes made of customary and proven materials in adequate diameters according to the amount of wastewater conducted in the pipes. In the case of geodetic constraints, pumping stations must be installed in adequate numbers. In the case of using cesspools, intermediate storage is allowed. The cesspools  must be emptied by vacuum loader(s), which are also part of the scope of supply.
The collected wastewater should be treated in accordance with the above effluent limits.
In order to meet the required quality of clarification, sanitary and domestic wastewater streams should at least be treated by screening and primary sedimentation, biological clarification in activated sludge basins, sedimentation for removing the activated sludge and as a last stage an effluent disinfection for discharging
the wastewater into the sea. The treated sanitary wastewater should also be used for irrigation purposes if required.
All wastewater streams discharged into the domestic waste water treatment plant shall be free of toxic and inhibitory compounds concerning the process of biological clarification or compounds that can influence the further use of the sewage sludge.
The sewage sludge should either be treated or dried for use as fertilizer or disposed of in a suitably designed landfill according to US EPA/EU specification.
In  order  to  meet  the  required  quality  values,  industrial  wastewater  should  be  treated  separately  with special regard to the parameters listed in Table above.
Special regard is to be paid by the Contractor to the contamination of the several streams and the adequacy and suitability of treatment process wastewater streams with similar contamination can be summarized and mixed before treatment. Oil contaminated water have to be treated in oil separators.

itb.keywords: WBG requirements, local solid waste management guidelines, liquid effluents from thermal power plants, IFC Thermal Power Guidelines 2008, pH 6-9, TSS 50 mg/L, oil and grease 10 mg/L, total residual chlorine 0.2 mg/L, heavy metals effluent limits (Cr, Cu, Pb, Cd, Hg, As, Zn, Fe), soil contamination prevention, oil and chemical spillage, terrestrial ecosystem impact prevention
itb.chunk_text:
The Project shall adhere to local solid waste management guidelines and implement the requirements of WBG for solid wastes and liquid wastes. Oil can become contaminated by oil and chemical spillage during construction,  operation  and  maintenance of  the  Plant.  The  entire  Plant  shall  be  designed,  constructed, operated and maintained in such a way that any soil contamination will be prevented.
The WBG standards liquid effluents originating from thermal power plants are summarised in Table below.
Effluents from Thermal Power Plants (IFC, Thermal Power Guidelines 2008)
pH, Maximum Value (Unit) = 6-9 (pH). TSS, Maximum Value (Unit) = 50 (mg/L). Oil and Grease, Maximum Value (Unit) = 10 (mg/L). Total Residual Chorine, Maximum Value (Unit) = 0.2 (mg/L). Chromium (Total), Maximum Value (Unit) = 0.5 (mg/L). Copper, Maximum Value (Unit) = 0.5 (mg/L). Iron, Maximum Value (Unit) = 1.0 (mg/L). Zinc, Maximum Value (Unit) = 1.0 (mg/L). Lead, Maximum Value (Unit) = 0.5 (mg/L). Cadmium (Cd), Maximum Value (Unit) = 0.1 (mg/L). Mercury (Hg), Maximum Value (Unit) = 0.005 (mg/L). Arsenic (As), Maximum Value (Unit) = 0.5 (mg/L)
The plant shall be designed, operated, and maintained in such a way to prevent any soil contamination or impact  on  the  terrestrial  ecosystem.  This  shall  be  in  line  with  the  environmental  and  social  impact assessment and RC permitting.

itb.keywords: RAM modelling objectives, capacity assumptions validation, unit and plant level, generation losses contributors, design inherent reliability, electrical power continuity of supply reliability, final plant design basis, sensitivity analysis, input parameters effect on reliability output, conditions/assumptions to maintain representative reliability, plant operation reliability, Operation & Maintenance stage impacts
itb.chunk_text:
The RAM modelling effort  has  several  objectives  based  on  the  activity's  timing  and  the  level  of  detail incorporated in the model.
The main goals of the RAM assessment shall be:
- To test the capacity assumptions used in the initial design documents, at the unit and plant level, and identified equipment, systems or other factors contributing to the generation losses
- To  calculate  the  design  inherent  reliability  of  the  plant  represented  by  electrical  power continuity  of  supply reliability,  based  on  the  final  design  of  the  plant,  including  a  sensitivity analysis  in  order  to  determine  the  effect  on  reliability  output  changes  in  the  different  input parameters
- Definition  of  conditions  or  assumptions  under  which  that  calculated  reliability  can  be maintained as representative of the 'reliability of the plant operation'. Especially the related considerations of aspects, additional to design, that affect to the final achievable reliability like those which would be in the scope in the Operation & Maintenance of the plant stage.

depths.3rd Depth: Monte Carlo RAM Modeling and RBD Development

itb.keywords: RAM assessment, Monte Carlo methodology, Isograph, EN 60812, Base Case Model, equipment reliability data, Reliability Block Diagrams (RBDs), system failure logic, redundancy modeling, failure modes and consequences, MTTF, MTTR, plant availability and reliability
itb.chunk_text:
The RAM assessment to be developed by the EPC Contractor and shall include the following:
- The RAM software to be employed to perform calculations shall be based on Monte Carlo methodology and performed using Isograph.
- International standard EN-60812 or similar shall be considered.
- Establish a Base Case Model with all assumptions, including equipment reliability data used in the assessment.
- Prepare  Reliability  Block  Diagrams  (RBDs),  including  but  not  limited  to  configuration, sparing, and sizing arrangements. The RBD shall accurately model the system failure logic and include all redundancy in each specific system.
- Prepare a list of equipment or systems considered in the model with the Failure Mode and Failure Rates included in the models (MTTF, MTTR).
- Prepare a Base Case Model analysis, providing recommendations for the improvement of overall  reliability.  Perform  sensitivity  analyses,  for  the  recommended  parameters  or equipment or for the client chosen parameters after analysing the first base case draft.
- Model uncertainty related to equipment failure, to prevent potential effects on the process and identify appropriate actions that will lead to reduced consequences
- RAM analysis shall be developed 'top-down' and expanded to lower levels.
- Expected average Plant availability and reliability
- Identification of all potential critical components and process bottlenecks
- Identification of failure modes and their consequences
- Decision  support  to  determine  the  most  cost-optimal  solution  to  improve  reliability results with respect to:
- Process design
- Spare part philosophy
- Mobilization times and contracts
- Preventive maintenance strategy
- Identification of cost-effective measures
- Knowledge of industry performance methodology

itb.keywords: auxiliary systems redundancy, no single auxiliary equipment failure or trip, no reduction of power capacity, critical auxiliary equipment N+1 configuration, station (common) auxiliaries redundancy, instantaneous start of redundant backup equipment, main equipment definition, GTs, HRSGs, STs, GRMS, condensers, generators, main transformers, aux transformers, major electrical equipment, cables, pre-treatment
itb.chunk_text: An appropriate level of redundancy shall be included in each auxiliary system. The Plant shall be designed so that no single auxiliary equipment failure or trip (except main equipment) shall result in the reduction of power capacity. In this context, it is required that all critical auxiliary equipment shall be provided with N+1  configuration.  Station  (common)  auxiliaries  shall  include  similar  redundancy  such  that  no  single equipment failure shall result in any loss of Plant generating capacity. Main equipment refers to all GTs, HRSGs,  STs,  GRMS,  condensers,  generators,  main  transformers,  aux.  transformers,  major  electrical equipment,  cables,  pre-treatment.  Redundant  backup  equipment  shall  start  instantaneously  to  enable continued functioning of the process without consequent malfunction.

itb.keywords: redundant pumps and compressors, on-line switchover capability, N+1 redundancy, 2x100% lube oil pump for HP feedwater pump, 2x100% lube oil heater for HP feedwater pump, power plant jockey pumps 2x100%, cooling tower / fin fan cooler cells N+1, condensate storage tank 2x50% or 1x100%, service air receiver tank 2x100%, instrument air receiver tank 2x100%, fuel gas boosting compressors N+1 (N = number of gas turbines), drain and vent valves two in series if pressure > 4 MPa
itb.chunk_text:
All  pumps  and  compressors  shall  be  redundant  with  on-line  switchover  capability  with  following redundancy:
- Pumps, blowers, compressors, fans : N+1
- Lube oil pump for HP Feedwater Pump : 2x100% (for each FW pump)
- Lube oil heater for HP Feedwater Pump : 2x100% (for each FW pump)
- Power Plant Jockey pumps : 2x100%
- Heat exchangers (not applicable to fin fan cooler or to air cooled condenser). Redundancy should be considered to eliminate single point of failure that will result in reduced load.
- Cooling tower/fin fan cooler cells : N+1
- Tanks (if not mentioned hereunder) : more than 1
- CCW Expansion Tanks : 1 x 100%
- Atmospheric drain tank : 1 x 100%
- Vacuum Flash Tank : 1 x 100%
- Condensate Storage Tank : 2x50% or 1x100%
- Service air receiver tank : 2 x 100%
- Instrument air receiver tank : 2 x 100%
- H2 Tanks : 2 x 50%
- Diesel storage tank : 2 x 50%
- Gas Drain Collection Tank (GT Area) : 1 x 100%
- GT Fuel Gas Last Chance Filter (per GT) : 2 x 100% Chemical tanks
- DM plant : N+1 stream
- Air conditioning :  N+1  (except  for  non-plant  buildings,  such  as: Administration building/ workshop/warehouse/Gate guard house)
- Ventilation Fans :  N+1  (except  for  non-plant  buildings,  such  as: Administration building/ workshop/warehouse/Gate guard house))
- Gas reducing station : 3 x 50%
- Feed water control stations : 2 x 100%
- Fuel Gas Boosting Compressors: : N+1, where, N=Number of Gas Turbines
- Air  compressors  with  after  coolers  (after  coolers  if  required,  will  be  confirmed  during  detail engineering) : 3x50%
- Air filtering skids : 2 x 100%
- Air dryers : 2 x 100%
- After Filters : 2 x 100%
- CO2 rack & manifold station for each GT : 1 x 100%
- CO2 rack & manifold station for each ST : 1 x 100%
- N2 rack & manifold station : 1 x 100%
- H2 generator : 2 x 100%
- Drain and vent valves :  two  valves  in  series  (If  operating  pressure  is greater than 4 MPa) otherwise single valve
- Level control valve for HRSG Drums and Feedwater tank :  N+1 (not applicable for startup line, as applicable)
Provision of bypass valves for control valves shall apply for those systems/facilities which can also be reasonably controlled manually.

itb.keywords: no single main equipment failure forced outage, no single auxiliary equipment failure forced derating, redundant auxiliary services power supply concept, redundant UATs, MV distributions redundancy, LV distributions redundancy, DC system redundancy, UPS system redundancy, protection system electronic devices redundancy, separate buses and physical segregation, automatic standby equipment activation, GT MCC double incoming CB, normal bus and essential busbar, bus-coupler
itb.chunk_text:
- No single main equipment (GTU, STU, GSUT and HRSG) failure shall result in a Forced Outage of the entire Plant.
- No single auxiliary equipment (all other equipment than main equipment as specified above) failure shall result in the Forced Derating of Plant. The compliance with the above criterion requires to a large extent  redundancy  of  the  entire  auxiliary  equipment.  Following  examples  shall  illustrate  this requirement:
- The Plant shall have a redundant power supply concept for the auxiliary services (redundant UATs, MV - distributions, LV- distributions, DC-system, UPS- system)
- Electronic devices of the protection systems must be redundant in case process redundancy is not available, while the requirement doesn't apply to MV&LV protection relay.
- Redundant active equipment shall be powered from separate buses and physically segregated where feasible. The system design shall be such that the standby equipment shall be activated automatically when the control system detects a failure of the running equipment to perform its intended function.
- GT MCC shall have the redundant / double incoming CB, and divided to two buses, normal bus and essential bus bar, with bus-coupler.

itb.keywords: MV and LV bus sections capacity, bus coupler load transfer on supply failure, N-1 redundancy for switchboard and MCC, transformer cooling fans redundancy, transformer oil pump redundancy, rated output within specified temperature rise, DC system 2 x 100% battery, DC system 2 x 100% battery chargers, UPS N+1 redundancy, LV switchboard two bus sections, two incomers, one bus-coupler, 1 x 100% capacity transformer per incomer, diesel generator N+1 (EDG cum BSDG), DG sizing for emergency shutdown during black start, battery starting system 1 x 100% for BSEDG, Hazard Risk Category (HRC) labeling, arc flash assessment study, NFPA 70, IEC standards, OEM standard design for GT package LV & DC distribution
itb.chunk_text:
- The capacity of MV, LV bus sections and the sources feeding the bus sections should be adequate to take the load of the other bus section when the bus coupler closes in case of supply failure to other bus section.
- The n-1 redundancy criteria shall be maintained for each switchboard/MCC.
- Redundancy shall be provided for cooling fans such that with one group of fan or oil pump out of service the transformer would deliver the rated output within the specified temperature rise.
- Battery and battery chargers shall be provided with N+ 1 redundancy. DC System contains 2 x 100 % Battery and 2 x 100 % Battery Chargers to meet the redundancy requirements.
- UPS shall be provided with N+ 1 redundancy.
- Each LV system switchboard shall consist of two bus sections with two incomers and one bus- coupler. Each incomer shall be supplied by 1x100% capacity transformer.
- Diesel Generator shall be provided with N+1 criteria, where EDG cum BSDG concept to be adopted. The DG sizing shall consider all possible scenarios, including emergency shutdown during black start operation. Emergency cum BSDG DG sets shall have the capability of testing even if respective block is in normal operation OR when the respective block switchgear bus have no voltage. 1 x 100% battery starting system will be applied for BSEDG.
- All electrical system switchboards shall be labelled for Hazard Risk category (HRC) as per results of ARC Flash assessment study using NFPA 70 or relevant IEC standards (as applicable).
- For Gas turbine package, redundancy concept of LV & DC distribution for equipment supplied by OEM would be of OEM's standard design.

itb.chunk_text:
Redundancy for control & instrumentation shall be as given below:
- All redundant instrumentation shall have the hot swap capability. Critical Redundant equipment shall be change over automatically in case of failure one equipment / Instrument. (For Gas turbine package, the hot swap capability is not applicable due to safety reason. Especially, it is not allowed to enter GT enclosure during operation, hence any person cannot access the instruments in GT enclosure.)
- Electronic modules in GT control system shall not be removed while the gas turbine is in operation.
- In general, devices shall be preferred that contain intrinsic safety, to avoid expensive supervision/monitoring installations, possibly subject to failure (In Gas turbine package, explosionproof type instruments will be used in the hazardous area.)
- Where redundant equipment is installed, it shall be possible to perform maintenance and repair works on one equipment while the others are in service.
- Hardware part of controls & instrumentation:
- Turbine GT/ST protection system (fail-safe and dual redundant system), For Gas turbine package GT Protection Panel which will consist of Tricon CX triple modular redundant safety PLC system by Schneider Electric Systems as per Supplier's standard design is considered.
- HRSG-protection (fail-safe and triple modular redundant for BMS)
- Triple redundant transmitters for Plant protection signals such as steam drum and main steam parameters.
- Critical measurements, which are supplied with redundant instrumentation shall be connected to different I/O cards.
- Software Protections:

depths.3rd Depth: Control and protection system redundancy and voting logic

itb.keywords: 2oo3 voting logic, 1oo2 voting logic, 2oo2 voting logic, generator protection system, multifunction protective relays (2), SIL study, IEC 61508, IEC 61511, redundant control supplies, redundant DC source, UPS redundant AC source, DCS redundancy (processor, power supply, network, server, I/O)
itb.chunk_text:
- All protection signals leading to a trip of the Plant or to a load reduction shall use 2 out of 3 voting logic. For Generator Protection System, signal shall be achieved through 1 out of 2 with two multifunction protective relays shall be provided for generator.
- Other controls can be achieved through 2oo2 or 1oo2 voting as per OEM's recommendations.
- Protection for people and environment shall be considered in SIL study according to IEC 61508 and IEC 61511. Allocation of the safety related function (the SIL loop) and its SIL level will be determined according to result of the SIL study.
- All  control  panels,  control  systems  shall  be  provided  with  redundant control supplies. Control and Protection Panels shall be fed from either two redundant DC Source or redundant AC Source (UPS). So, in case of failure one source, the second standby source will take over automatically and will not have any power interruption. (For Gas turbine package, the power supply of GT control system will be fed from essential AC and DC system as per Supplier's standards and power supply for the Gas turbine equipment and CCR will be fed from UPS.)
- Unit protection shall preferably be independently implemented in separate hardware to the control system(s)  to  avoid  common  mode  failure  and  with  appropriate  redundancy  to  ensure  security  of operation.
- For redundancy provisions of equipment, no single fault within the control system shall cause the failure of the duty equipment and at the same time cause the standby equipment to be unavailable.
- Redundancy in the DCS shall include
- Processer redundancy
- Power supply redundancy
- Network redundancy
- Server redundancy
- I/O card segregation
- I/O  card  redundancy  for  critical  signals  (each  of  the  1oo2  or  2oo3  redundant  signals  will  be hardwired to different I/O cards, with each cabinet having redundant power supplies)
- In the case of redundant signals are connected to the different cards, redundant I/O cards are not required.

Performance correction curves and formulae for the correction of measured performance data at conditions different from the Reference Conditions shall be provided by the contractor for both the primary and the backup fuel:
- Gas Turbine Standard correction curves
- Gas Turbine generator capability curve
- Steam Turbine generator capability curve
- CC Start-up curves
- CC Shutdown curve
- Capacity of GT system vs ambient temperature
- Gas Turbine GSUT capacity curve
- Response capability curve (frequency response chart)
- Emissions table
- Steam turbine load changes
- Power output vs gas pressure
- CC Correction curves (to be provided for):
- Evaporative Cooler ON (Only for Base Load),
- Wet Compression On (only after Evaporative Cooler is ON)
- Evaporative Cooler OFF (Base Load and partial loads)
- Duct Firing On (if applicable)
- o The corrections of the net capacity and net heat rate of the total Plant in combined cycle configuration shall be provided for:
- ambient air temperature
- ambient air humidity
- ambient barometric pressure
- Fuel Gas Lower Heating value (LHV)
- Fuel Gas C:H ratio
- Inlet  Air  Condition  Difference  Between  Cooling  Tower/ACC  and  Gas Turbine
- Grid Frequency
- Power Factor
- Cycle Unaccounted Losses
- Natural Gas Pressure at the Terminal Point
- Natural Gas Temperature at the Terminal Point
- Partial load (only for EVC OFF case)
- Degradation with GT fired hours
- condensate return flow and temperature
- b. Outage modes
The important and different outage modes encountered during the operation shall be furnished by the Contractor. Corresponding H&M balance drawings are to be supplied by the Contractor.
The outage durations of GT, HRSG and ST shall be defined.
The  outage  frequency  shall  be  defined  for  HRSG,  ST  and  GT  (in  line  with  the  typical  LTSA assumptions).

depths.3rd Depth: Civil engineering design scope and design life

itb.keywords: civil engineering design responsibility, architectural design, structural design, building services design, temporary and permanent works, minimum working life 50 years, main structural elements, secondary structural elements/cladding, building services: electricity, telephone, computer, water, HVAC, fire protection, maintenance accessibility and clearance from structural members and foundations, external building materials durability, sandstorm erosion, saline and corrosive environment, pipe/underground cable crossings under roads and railroads, O&M maintenance access without disturbing traffic
itb.chunk_text:
The Contractor is responsible for all aspects of civil engineering design. This shall include architectural, civil, structural and building services design for all temporary and permanent works. The civil works shall be designed to have a minimum working life of fifty (50) years before any significant repair or replacement of the main structural elements and secondary structural elements/cladding. This section identifies the Owner's minimum design requirements and parameters that are to be provided by the C ontractor.
The  Contractor  shall  provide  all  building  services  (electricity,  telephone,  computer,  water,  HVAC,  fire protection  etc.)  and  ensure  that  they  are  readily  accessible  for  maintenance  and  repair  and  adequate clearance is provided from main structural members and foundations.
The choice of external building materials shall be durable against sandstorm erosion, saline and corrosive environment.
Any pipe or underground cables crossings outside the plant boundary under Roads and Railroads shall be designed and constructed such that, proper access for maintenance of the damaged part can be possible during O&M period without disturbing the traffics under Roads and Railroads.

itb.keywords: backfill compaction 75% relative density, backfill compaction 85% relative density, ASTM D 4253, ASTM D 4254, ASTM D 1557 maximum density, 75 micron sieve, <15% fines non plastic material, >15% material passing 75 micron sieve, cap layer wind erosion protection, cap layer 150 mm thick, soil-cement asphalt paving / polymer-based erosion inhibitors, geotextile layer between filling and soil
itb.chunk_text:
Backfill placed for embankments, non-supportive and unpaved areas shall be compacted to at least 75% relative density (ASTM D 4253 and ASTM D 4254) for free draining soils containing less than 15% by weight finer than 75 micron sieve non plastic material or 90% of the maximum density as determined by ASTM D 1557for soils containing more than 15% material passing the 75 micron sieve.
Backfill placed below all the supports, roads and paved areas shall be minimum compacted to 85% relative density (ASTM D 4253 and ASTM D 4254) for free draining soils containing less than 15% by weight finer than 75 micron sieve non plastic material or 95% of the maximum density as determined by ASTM D 1557 for soils containing more than 15% material passing the 75 micron sieve.
A cap layer shall be placed to provide wind erosion protection in all the outdoor exposed areas. The cap layer shall be a minimum of 150 mm thick. The contractor to use soil-cement asphalt paving or sprayed-on polymer-based erosion inhibitors on that capping layer. Gravel layer is acceptable, as long as no erosion possibility is there due to water and wind. Gravel layer thickness 100 mm can be considered. However, this is subject to the Geotechnical recommendation.
For the design purpose, Design Ground water level shall be considered as per Geotechnical information, however  seasonal  variation  of  groundwater  and  capillary  rise  of  groundwater  shall  be  taken  into  the consideration for design and construction work and shall be substantiated before the start of design and construction work.
No foundations shall be supported on backfilled soil. Only less important and lighter foundation can be rested on backfilled soil subject to detail engineering and Owner's approval fulfilling the settlement requirement.
A  geotextile  layer  shall  be  put  between  the  filling  layer  and  the  soil  after  removal  of  top  layer  if recommended by EPC Geotechnical study.

itb.chunk_text:
Selected fill shall have the following properties:
Well graded having uniformity index of not less than 5. Selected fill shall be non-cohesive, free of plastic clays and having silt content not greater than 5%, salt content less than 3% and organic matter not greater than 2%. Decomposing or compressible materials shall not be acceptable.
The material shall be of such nature and character that it can be compacted to the specified densities. It shall be free of all materials subject to decay, decomposition or dissolution, and of cinders or other material that will corrode piping or other material.
The intention is to use selected fill below structures, below pipelines, backfill to structures, roads, parking areas and hard standings etc.

depths.3rd Depth: Soil stabilization and slope erosion control

itb.keywords: soil stabilization with cement, soil-cement mixture, moisture conditioned within 1% of optimum moisture, compaction 98% of maximum dry density, ASTM D-558, Type V Portland Cement, ASTM C 150, erosion control blankets, fibre rolls (logs), coir logs / rice-wheat straw logs, Tensar type geo-grids, gravel layer thickness 100 mm
itb.chunk_text:
If the surface soils is susceptible to wind and water erosion these shall be stabilized with Cement. The soil and cement should be well mixed, moisture conditioned to within 1 per cent of optimum moisture and compacted to at least 98% of the maximum dry density. The optimum moisture content and maximum dry density of the soil-cement mixture should be determined by the ASTM D-558 test method. Traffic, except as required to maintain the surface of the soil cement in a damp condition, should not be permitted for at least 24 hours after final compaction.
For slope protection against erosion from wind, stabilization of surface soil with Type V Portland Cement as per ASTM C 150 may be adopted. For slope protection against erosion from water, slowing down of surface water is needed. To accomplish this, erosion control blankets, fibre rolls may be used. Erosion control blankets are usually woven type from a chosen material, with lots of ridges and obstructions. These materials are either synthetic or natural. Fibber rolls are also made of similar material as used in erosion control blankets but are rolled into large diameter logs. Coir type logs/ Logs made of rice/wheat straw also may be used. These logs are nailed into the slope to slow down the surface water. Tensar type geo-grids also may be effective. The source/ availability of the appropriate material is essential in selection of the technique, and it shall be duly approved by the Owner's engineer.
Gravel layer is acceptable, as long as no erosion possibility is there due to water and wind. Gravel layer thickness 100 mm can be considered.

itb.chunk_text:
The safe working capacity of the pile(s) shall be determined by calculation using recognized soil mechanic principles and equations. The Contractor shall carry out a programme of preliminary test piling at site to verify his designs prior to commencing the installation of permanent 'working' piles. The maximum load applied during the preliminary pile testing programme shall be 200% of pile working load. The settlement limit in this case shall follow relevant applicable International/local standards. Upon completion of testing preliminary piles shall be cut down and abandoned, such piles may not be incorporated into the permanent works construction.
For the structural design of the piles the recommendations in ACI 318M-08/318RM08: 'Metric Building Code Requirements for Structural Concrete and Commentary' and ACI 543R -00 Design, Manufacture and Installation of Concrete Piles and the requirements of this OTS shall be followed.
Permissible pile settlements at under load for compression, tension and lateral load tests shall not exceed settlement criteria imposed by plant manufacturers, local regulations or shall conform with the BS 8004, whichever is the most stringent. With ys, sls >= 1.0, the settlement of an individual pile shall be limited to less than 3% of its diameter, D; with 1.2, the settlement shall he limited to less than 1.5% D complying BS 8004 requirements.
If piles are required to resist dynamic loads they shall not be loaded to more than 50% and 85% of their safe working load during normal (dead, live and other sustain load) and abnormal operating conditions (wind, seismic and other transient load) respectively.
The design of the foundations for plant subject to dynamic loads shall be in accordance with DIN 4024 : Part 1 (1988) 'Machine Foundations' and CP 2012 : Part 1 'Foundations for Reciprocating Machines'. If manufacturer's design guide is not coincided with above mentioned code, then manufacturer's guide shall be considered preferentially
The bearing pressure under foundations subject to dynamic loads shall not exceed 60% and 90% of the safe ground bearing pressure during normal and abnormal operating conditions respectively.
The  overall  and  differential  settlement  of  foundations  for  plant  shall  strictly  adhere  to  the  plant manufacturer's requirements or accepted standards which is more stringent.
The allowable overall settlement for the isolated foundations shall not exceed 25 mm. The allowable overall settlement for the raft foundations shall not exceed 50 mm. The allowable differential settlement for the tanks  ring  beam  foundations  shall  be  designed  in  accordance  with  API  650.  The  allowable  overall settlement after the hydrotest for the tank foundations supported on ring beams shall not be more than 50mm.

itb.keywords: steam turbine building protection from environmental conditions, noise attenuation, non-combustible construction, dust proof building, ventilation; internal design temperature ≤ 5°C above maximum ambient, entrances sized for largest item access, lay-down areas for O&M, cranes capacity for maintenance of gas turbine auxiliaries (casing, rotor), access for single complete rotors; rotor unstacking area with suitable foundation, paved areas for mobile crane and low bed trailer, removable panels; roof walkways with railings and lighting, floor slab with pipe/cable trenches; floor drains to oily water separators; fire-rated steel doors; emergency exits with panic bars
itb.chunk_text:
The Steam turbine buildings shall provide protection of the equipment, electrical enclosed installation and controls from the environmental conditions. The buildings shall be designed for noise attenuation and be of non-combustible construction. The buildings shall be dust proof type and ventilated so that the building internal Design Temperature should not be greater than 5°C above maximum ambient temperature. The entrances shall be sufficiently sized to provide access for the largest item to be located within respective Building.
The  building  shall  be  of  sufficient  size  to  facilitate  the  installation  operation  and  maintenance  of  all components and equipment housed therein.  Requisite lay-down areas shall be provided for O&M purpose. Entrances shall be suitably sized and located to facilitate maintenance requirements.
Proper handling arrangement shall be provided for the equipment for O&M period.
Sufficient  capacities  of  cranes  shall  be  erected  for  normal  maintenance  of  the  gas  turbine  auxiliaries, including lifting heavy parts such as the casing and rotor.
Suitable access to the turbine building shall be provided to allow access for single complete rotors. A rotor unstacking area shall be provided with a suitable foundation to enable unstacking of a single rotor in the upright position and all necessary equipment shall be provided to manoeuvre and support the rotor. The turbine laydown/maintenance area may also function as the rotor unstacking area; however the Contractor shall take due care of the space usage and functionality.
Suitable  paved  areas  outside  the  Turbine  Buildings  to  put  the  mobile  crane  and  a  low  bed  trailer,  for transportation of the disassembled parts, in a stable way.
The separate turbine enclosures will be foreseen with easily removable panel(s) that can be lifted by the crane and can be put aside and foresee walkways with railings, sufficient lighting, around the roof and around the roof opening(s) that, with a connection in between the walkways.
The separate turbine enclosure shall be foreseen with removable  beams to connect hoists in strategic locations, such as above the combustion chambers.
The floor slab within the building, which incorporates pipe and cable trenches shall be constructed of reinforced concrete laid flat and with local dishing incorporated adjacent to floor gully inlets. Floor drains shall discharge via a piped drainage network into oily water separators. Trench covers shall be designed to accept the appropriate floor loading according to their location and shall be manually removable.
Emergency exits fitted with panic escape bars shall be provided to all areas of the turbine buildings and annexes and boiler enclosures. Steel doors and frames should comply with the fire rating requirements. These openings must be kept clear of all obstructions.

itb.keywords: Gas Turbine (GT) foundation, Steam Turbine (ST) foundation, monolithic raft foundation, piles (per Geotechnical report), exhaust stack foundation (separate or incorporated), minimum rebar content 80 kg/m3 concrete, machine foundation design code, ACI 351, CP 2012 internal reinforcement cage system, holding down bolts anchoring system, DIN 4024 dynamic analysis
itb.chunk_text:
The GT and ST foundations shall be a monolithic raft supported by piles  if required as per the Geotechnical report.  The  exhaust  stack  may  be  supported  by  a  separate  foundation  or  incorporated  within  the foundation if required by the Contractor.
The contractor shall ensure that the following points are included in the GT and ST foundation works:
- a. A minimum rebar content of 80 kg/m 3  of concrete shall be provided.
- b. The design of the GT and ST foundation shall satisfy, in addition to an appropriate internationally recognized design code on machine foundations, the following codes: ACI 351,  CP 2012 and DIN 4024. CP 2012  requires an  internal  reinforcement cage system which is essential for the foundation to act as a homogenous mass and provide a second line of defence to the machine anchoring system with the holding down bolts. DIN 4024 provides guidelines for carrying out dynamic analysis.

itb.keywords: GT and ST foundation isolation by floor joints, foundation mass ratio minimum 2 (foundation to GT/ST plant mass), pile load limit 60% working capacity (normal conditions), pile load limit 90% working capacity (extreme conditions), allowable soil bearing capacity limits 60% normal / 90% extreme, thermal effects and extreme differential temperatures on foundations, protective measures during construction (thermal), below-ground coating system for sulphate soils and groundwater chlorides, corrosion protection of reinforcement due to chloride ion content, foundation poured in one operation; construction joints not permitted, dynamic modelling of bearing points, foundation and soil body (coupling/interaction), table top structure and columns over mat foundation; springs isolation
itb.chunk_text:
- c. The GT and ST foundation shall be isolated from the rest of the works by floor joints.
- d. The ratio of mass of the foundation to mass of the GT and ST plant shall be at least 2.
- e. To reduce the risk of dynamic compaction the maximum load on any pile supporting a GT and ST foundation shall not exceed 60 per cent of its working capacity during the normal operating conditions and shall not exceed 90 per cent in extreme conditions. For a foundation supported by soil the same limits apply to the allowable bearing capacity of the soil.
- f. The design  of  the  GT  and  ST  foundations  shall  include  the  thermal  effects  on  the foundation and its ability to withstand the extreme differential temperatures likely to be experienced by the foundation, during the construction as well as throughout its design life. Protective measures during construction shall be part of the design.
- g. The section  of  the  GT  and  ST  foundation  below  ground  shall  be  protected  with  a coating system to resist attack from the sulphate content in the soils and chlorides from the ground water. Further protection against corrosion of the reinforcement (which leads to expansion of the concrete and cracking) due to the severe chloride ion content of the soils and groundwater shall be provided as covered by the concrete section of this Specification.
- h. The GT and ST foundation shall be poured in one operation and construction joints are not permitted unless in exceptional circumstances and with the approval of the Owner/Owner's Engineer.
- i. The design, detailing and construction of the GT and ST foundations shall allow fully for  the  'buildability'  of  the  foundations,  particularly  where  congested  areas  of reinforcement are required.
- j. In addition to the static structural design the contractor shall prove the design of the turbine  supporting  structure  dynamically  by  modelling  the  bearing  points,  the foundation and the soil body together, taking the full consideration of the coupling effect and interaction between the three systems.
- k. The  design  of  turbine  supporting  structures,  if  applicable,  shall  be  same  as  that supporting the gas turbines except in some designs a table top structure and columns are erected over a mat foundation. The supporting structure if cast monolithically shall  be  analysed  with  due  consideration  of  the  flexibility  of  each  structural component.  If the table top structure is supported by springs the substructure may be  designed  as  a  static  structure  if  its  superstructure  proves  a  sufficient  isolation achieved by the springs.
The Contractor shall submit thermal curing procedures for the steam turbine and gas turbine foundations to the Owner/Owner's Engineer for approval prior to commencing construction of these works.

itb.keywords: cavities and voids probing, supplementary ground investigation studies, grout injection for cavities/voids, piled foundations for major structures and buildings, settlement criteria, BS 5930:1999 site investigations (Section 12.7.2), geophysical tests at key foundations, dewatering methodology fit for purpose, restrict movement of fine grain material below foundation level, pressure bulbs overlap (surrounding foundations), maximum differential settlement 1/500 rad, settlement monitoring system, steam and gas turbines foundations (key foundation)
itb.chunk_text:
The Contractor shall pay especial attention for the unknown amount of cavities, voids and interconnecting discontinuities  and  shall  ensure  that  the  locations  of  all  significant  plant  and  building  foundations  are thoroughly probed for voids and discontinuities as part of his supplementary ground investigation studies.
To mitigating the settlement risk the cavities and voids may be grouted injected if they are found below the major foundations. Alternately the foundations may be founded on piles.
The design of piled foundations for major structures and buildings shall conform to the settlement criteria stated earlier of the specification.
Following activities are mandatory for the Foundation design and construction:
- The depth of the Borehole shall be considered based on following criteria as a minimum: British  Standard:  Code  of  practice  for  site  investigations  BS  5930:1999  Section '12.7.2 Foundations for structures
- Geophysical tests at the key foundations (to be agreed with Owner) locations to be carried out before the construction/erection of foundations
- If cavities are found, required soil improvement/ foundation design criteria to be carried out subject to OE approval.
- Dewatering methodology will have to be demonstrated is fit for purpose according to soil conditions and submitted for Owner approval. Particular attention to be paid to those soils that can be degraded and/or settled due to dewatering process.
- Dewatering  shall  ensure  to  restrict  the  movement  of  fine  grain  material  below  the foundation level.
- The  dewatering  work  shall  be  performed  with  reputed  local  Specialize  contractor.  The
- Contractor for dewatering and the Dewatering process shall be approved by the Owner. Dewatering design shall be submitted for owner's approval. Following criteria shall be given special consideration while designing the foundation:
- Effect of surrounding foundations shall be considered when pressure bulbs supposed to be overlapping. For key foundations raft foundations will be prefer design criteria.
- During  construction  EPC  will  take  measurement  of  settlement  and  send  a  result  that differential settlement within the limit complying with OEM requirement is achieved.
•
- Detail geotechnical analysis will have to be performed by EPC contractor by a first class engineer for the key foundations as a detail input of the main foundation design.
- Main foundations design basis will be subject to Owner approval.
- Foundation  design  will  obviously  consider  all  the  applicable  loads  including  backfilling, foundation weights, dead and live load, equipment dead load and dynamic loads, hydrostatic load, environmental load and any other load as applicable.
- Maximum Differential settlement value for the foundations shall be submitted for Owners approval  and  as  a  general  criteria  1/500  rad.  or  as  per  Equipment  manufacturer's recommendation whichever is stringent shall be followed.
- Foundation designs will have to comply with applicable local regulations including local, municipality and country applicable regulations.
- Settlement monitoring system shall be considered for the key foundations.
•
Following foundations shall be considered as Key foundation:
- Steam and Gas Turbines foundations

itb.keywords: local regulations, AASHTO requirements, road network design, accessibility to offshore facilities and on-shore plant, interfaces with existing road network, security protection and safety, road system to serve all buildings, raised kerbs, surface water drainage system, gullies or catch pits with grating, 25 years design period, reinforced concrete roads, flexible bituminous concrete asphalt minimum two layers, oil spillage areas heavy and abnormal loading, sidewalks, main and secondary access gate, main and minor gate house
itb.chunk_text:
Design and construction standards and criteria for roads shall be in accordance with the local regulations and AASHTO requirements.
The final road network design shall incorporate two major considerations:
- Full  accessibility  to  the  offshore  facilities  and  on-shore  plant  ensuring  that  all  operational  and maintenance requirements can be fulfilled in an efficient manner including interfaces with the existing road network;
- Security, protection and safety of the employees and the Plant
A road system shall be provided to serve all buildings on the Site.
The roads shall be constructed between raised kerbs and graded to falls leading surface water into gullies or catch pits that will connect into the surface water drainage system. Gullies shall be provided with grating to prevent the ingress of debris into the drains.
Road pavements are to be designed to for a 25 years design period.
The roads shall be constructed in reinforced concrete or in flexible bituminous concrete (asphalt minimum of two layers) construction, depending upon the location. Concrete roads shall be used in areas of heavy and  abnormal  loading,  where  oil  spillage  may  occur  and  where  a  durable  and  maintenance  free construction  is  essential  to  the  movement  of  plant  and  equipment.  All  other  roads  shall  be  of  flexible construction with a bituminous concrete (asphalt) finish.
Sidewalk shall be provided for all the roads where it is necessary to satisfy person's walking requirement.
.
Main and Secondary Access Gate and Main and Minor Gate house shall be considered for entry/exit the plant.

itb.keywords: internal fences, doors and gates, 3 level master key security system, Grand Master key, HCIS Category -1, straining posts, maximum 60 m intervals (straight fence lengths), intermediate posts maximum 3 m centre-to-centre, mechanized vehicular gates double opening, gate swing 180°, emergency opening mechanical push bars (personnel gates), sand preventing arrangement / sand fence
itb.chunk_text:
Internal fences for the safety of any particular installation within the Plant Site shall be erected completely with all necessary doors and gates. The American standards may be used in addition to the local code.
Each type of internal fencing shall suit the level of security required by each installation. In general, each level of security shall be agreed with the Owner, however a 3 level master key security system shall be provided as a minimum.
Straining posts shall be provided at all ends and corners, at changes in direction or acute variations in level and at intervals of not more than 60m in straight lengths of fence. Struts shall be fitted to all straining posts, in the direction of each line of fencing. Steel struts and posts shall be bolted together. Intermediate posts shall be provided at intervals, measured centre-to-centre, of not more than 3m.
All building doors, equipment room or container doors and fence gate lock keys shall be operable by Grand Master key and to the approval of the Owner.
As per NFPA regulations, transformer shall be enclosed by fire walls. The entrance side shall be provided with a removable security internal fence fitted with a lockable personnel access gate compatible with Master key system.
The plant Area and sub-station area shall been closed by fence or  wall meeting the national and local guidelines. The plant fence or walls shall be maintained throughout the construction phase and at no time security of any of the plant sites shall be compromised. The fencing shall be HCIS Category -1.
The design of the fences, gates , boundary walls and all other security installations shall follow the local requirements. Internal fences for the safety of any particular installation within the Plant Site shall be erected completely with all necessary doors and gates. The American standards may be used in addition to the local code.
Internal fencing shall suit the level of security required by each installation. In general each level of security shall  be  agreed  with  the  Owner,  however  a  3  level  master  key  security  system  shall  be  provided  as  a minimum.
Mechanized Vehicular gates shall be double opening. Gates shall be furnished with hinges of a type which prevent the easy removal of gates from the gate posts. Gate hinges shall allow the gate to swing through 180°.  The  gates  shall  use  the  same  type  of  wire  mesh  as  used  for  the  fencing.  Emergency  opening mechanical push bars shall be provided to all personnel gates. Locking bars shall be provided to all vehicle gates and provision made for the attachment of a padlock which shall be accessible from both sides of the gate.
Hazards areas like transformer, fuel areas shall be protected with the internal fence and gate.
All building doors, equipment room or container doors and fence gate lock keys shall be operable by Grand Master key and to the approval of the Owner.
Sand preventing arrangement/sand fence shall be provided as required for the smooth operation of the plant to prevent the ingress of sand. The structural design of the fence shall consider loads if any from the deposited sand.

itb.keywords: 150 mm concrete paving, 1.2 m concrete apron from building edge, asphalt paving 1.2 m to 5.0 m (erosion-prone soil), slope to Surface Water Drainage System, separate collection, treatment and disposal of surface water runoff, roof drainage connected to surface water drainage system, storm water drainage design for 100-year rainfall return period, basement, cable and pipe trench and tunnel drainage to sumps, permanent/portable sump pumps for trench or tunnel sump pump-out, fire deluge water to storm water catch pits (prevent entry to tunnels), primary site drainage and sub-soil drainage (external areas), API and NFPA requirements for hazardous environments (storm water sump pumps/electrical)
itb.chunk_text:
All buildings in the Plant shall be paved with minimum 150 mm concrete extending from the edge of the building  for  a  distance  of  1.2m  with  proper  slope  to  drainage  Surface  Water  Drainage  System  and additionally asphalted paving shall be extending from 1.2 m up to a distance of 5.0m with proper slope to drainage Surface Water Drainage System if the soil is erosion prone due to water and wind.
A surface water drainage system shall be provided for the Plant. The design shall allow for the separate collection, treatment and disposal of surface water over the whole of the Site (arising from run-off of natural water from buildings, roads, ground surface, paved areas, etc.). All buildings shall be provided with roof drainage for disposal of surface water, and be connected to the surface water drainage system. The surface water drainage system shall be arranged and designed to effectively manage all run-off and discharge arising from the Site.
The Storm  water  Drainage  system  shall  be  designed  considering  100  years  rainfall  return  period  and rainfall intensity equal to the retention period.
Basements, cable and pipe trenches and tunnels shall be constructed with adequate provision for drainage. Floors to basements, trenches and tunnels shall be laid to falls and/or drainage channels provided therein. Any water entering the basements trenches or tunnels shall be routed to sumps and connected to the surface water drainage system. Where connection to the surface water drainage system is not practical, then provision to pump-out water from the trench or tunnel drainage sump, by permanent and/or portable sump pumps shall be made. Fire deluge water shall be gathered into storm water catch pits and discharged via main storm water system and prevented from entering tunnels.
Primary site drainage and sub-soil drainage shall be provided, where necessary, on external areas generally to protect the site from run off into building areas etc.
Storm water drainage sumps, pumps and electrical equipment shall be located to avoid hazardous areas. If unavoidable then the pumps and electrical equipment shall conform to the requirements in accordance with API and NFPA for operation in hazardous environments. Pumps shall be able to be withdrawn from the sump at surface level for maintenance and repair. The sump and valve chamber shall be equipped with access covers and ladders for maintenance purposes. The sump chamber shall be designed hydraulically so as not to impair pump performance.
Additionally,  ESIA  requirement  shall  be  completely  followed  for  storm  water  design  including  for  the requirement of Storm water basin.

depths.3rd Depth: Zero Liquid Discharge and wastewater treatment concept

itb.keywords: wastewater drainage system design, Environmental Regulations compliance, Zero Liquid Discharge (ZLD), uncontaminated storm water discharge only, evaporation pond, sludge disposal, wastewater treatment plant concept, maximum and normal flows, dedicated sump neutralisation, transformer compound oil spillage separation facilities, main building plant drainage, HRSG cleaning effluent and HRSG blowdown
itb.chunk_text:
The  Contractor  shall  be  responsible  for  design  of  wastewater  drainage  system  complying  with  the Environmental Regulations and other applicable regulations with respect to wastewater. The Contractor shall provide the following to comply with local environmental protection requirements.
The Plant shall be designed with Zero Liquid Discharge (ZLD) which means that no emissions of liquid effluents  other  than  uncontaminated  storm  water  will  be  discharged  to  the  environment.  Hence,  all wastewaters will be directed to an evaporation pond  where the accumulating sludge will regularly be disposed.
The Contractor shall present a concept for the wastewater treatment plants and demonstrate the major waste water treatment steps including the corresponding maximum and normal flows.
Treated waste waters from operations that are known to produce effluents will be directed to a dedicated sump  where  they  can  be  neutralised  before  being  pumped  to  an  evaporation  pond.  Transformer compounds: provide storage contamination and separation facilities for oil spillage;
- Main building plant drainage: oil spillage, effluent from HRSG cleaning, HRSG blowdown, air heater wash  and  other  non-oily  contaminated  sources,  provide  oil  separators,  chemical  treatment  and sedimentation facilities/evaporation pond.
The treated effluent shall be discharged by pumping or gravity, ultimately to the final discharge point.
Effluent discharged from station processes shall be treated to comply with local environmental protection requirements. Effluent discharged from station processes into the chemical drains, dirty drains and clean drains shall be routed directly, after treatment, to the final discharge point.

depths.2nd Depth: Sanitary Wastewater and Sewage Drainage System

itb.keywords: sanitary wastewater and sewage drainage system, separate collection of foul water (toilets, urinals, sinks), straight lines between manholes, self-cleansing drainage, access for rodding entire drainage system, package type sewage treatment plant, temporary and permanent drainage discharges compliance, plant internal reuse for irrigation, sludge used as fertilizer, PME/NCEC General Environmental Regulations and Rules for Implementation, inspection manholes every 60 m, 72 hour holding capacity without overflow
itb.chunk_text:
A sanitary wastewater and sewage drainage system shall be provided to allow for the separate collection, treatment and disposal of foul water (arising from toilets, urinals, sinks, etc.).
The sanitary wastewater and sewage drainage system shall be laid in straight lines between manholes. The systems  shall  be  self-cleansing  and  function  with  the  minimum  of  maintenance,  and  access  shall  be provided so that it is possible to rod the whole of the drainage system. The effluent shall be directed to a self-contained package type sewage treatment plant. The quality of all temporary and permanent drainage discharges from the Site shall comply with the local authority requirements.
Sanitary  wastewater  shall,  to  the  extent  possible,  be  plant  internally  re-used  after  its  treatment  for irrigation purposes. Its sludge shall be used, if applicable, as fertilizer.
For this reuse, the PME's/NCEC's General Environmental Regulations and Rules for Implementation apply. The sewage system shall consist of a piping system with inspection manholes every  60 m and at each change of direction
The piping  and  collection  system  shall  provide  holding  capacity  adequate  for  a  72  hour  failure  of  the treatment system without overflow.

depths.3rd Depth: Underground storage tank leak prevention and detection

itb.keywords: underground storage tank (UST), petroleum products, hazardous substances, avoid underground tank installation, impervious liner, concrete vault, double-walled tank, monitoring ports (lowest point), leak detection between walls, tank gauging (material volume), automatic fill shutoff valve, level overflow alarm to continuously attended workstation (control room)
itb.chunk_text:
Providing  of  any  underground  storage  tank  of  any  size  designed  to  contain  petroleum  products  or Hazardous Substances should be avoided. If underground installations is deemed necessary, all such tanks shall:
- Be provided in an impervious liners or structures (e.g. concrete vault) under or around tanks and lines that direct any leaked product to monitoring ports at the lowest point of the liner or structure or constructed with double walls; and
- Be provisioned with gauges to measure the material volume inside the tank for reconciling tank content, leak detection, automatic fill shutoff valves and level overflow alarms that are transmitted to a continuously attended workstation (e.g. from the Control room).
Impervious  liners  or  structures  shall  be  fabricated  of  material  appropriate  for  the  substance  being contained in the underground storage tanks. If a double walled tank is provided, means shall be provided to detect leaks between the walls.
Contractor shall report to the Owner why an underground tank is proposed and how its design meets Owner's minimum requirements for underground tank installation and operation.

itb.keywords: unload/load areas, transportation vehicles (tank trucks), liquid hazardous substances, petroleum products, impervious secondary spill containment, controlled rainwater drainage, lockable drain valve, containment capacity 110% of largest spill, freeboard 250 mm, check valve, leak-proof piping connections, transfer pipe system, back-up fuel oil tanks, reinforced concrete ring foundations, oil and water tight tank basin, oil proof coating
itb.chunk_text:
All areas used to unload/load transportation vehicles (e.g. tank, trucks) of liquid hazardous substances or petroleum products shall be provisioned with impervious secondary spill containment provisioned with a means to drain accumulated rain water  in  a  controlled  fashion  (i.e.  using  a  lockable  drain  valve).  The capacity of the impervious spill containment system must be capable of containing one hundred ten percent (110%) of the largest spill (e.g., truck capacity) and a free board of 250mm. Check valve and leak-proof piping connections shall be used for the transfer pipe system to prevent a release in the event of a system failure.
Back-up Fuel oil tanks shall be placed on reinforced concrete ring foundations and be located inside a oil and water tight tank basin of reinforced concrete slabs and surrounding walls with respective oil proof coating.

itb.chunk_text:
FRP Pipeline
In  addition  to  the  requirements  provided  hereunder,  the  EPC  Contractor  shall  follow  ACWA's  FRP Management system document.
Proper Geotextile layer shall be provided for the FRP pipe trenches to ensure no loss of fine particles are possible from pipe surrounding and pipe bed material. Sufficient gap shall be kept between the pipe edge and trench to allow proper compaction.
When a  valve  is  connected  to  a  FRP  pipeline,  expansion  bellows  are  to  be  considered  helps  in  valve replacement and maintenance without cutting the pipelines. The final locations of bellows shall be decided during detail engineering stage subject to Owner's approval.
AWWA M45 shall be followed for the installation of FRP pipes. All fibre glass pipe joints shall be laminated, complying  with  the  manufacturer's  recommendation  and  the  relevant  internationally  applicable  and accepted codes and standards.

itb.keywords: FRP pipe joints, onshore FRP pipeline laying, backfilling and bedding material quality, FRP pipe trench sizing, overburden loading, pipe stiffness value, in-situ installation and testing supervision, deflection and gap measurement, thrust blocks (concrete pipe thrust restraints/anchors), neoprene pad for concrete encasement, sleeve/trench road crossing (no weight transfer), permanent markers for underground utilities (cable duct banks, direct buried cables, pipes)
itb.chunk_text:
- The final  locations  of  bellows  shall  be  decided  during  detail  engineering  stage  subject  to  Owner's approval.
- The stiffness value has to be ascertained carefully depending on the route and overburden loading.
- Heavy Vehicle routes to be marked clearly with labels and signage.
- A specialized independent third party shall be appointed by the Contractor with the approval of the Owner for design review and Supervision of in-situ installation and testing.
- Following requirement shall be considered as mandatory.
- The specialized independent third party to review and approve the type of joints for the FRP pipe.
- The specialized independent third party to supervise of laying of FRP onshore pipeline.
- The specialized independent third party to review and approve the design for FRP pipeline installation and  backfilling,  MoS  for  the  laying  of  FRP  pipeline  including  the  backfilling  and  bedding  material quality, FRP Pipe trench sizing and type of FRP pipe joints.
- The  specialized  independent  third  party  to  involve  in  measurement  of  deflection  and  gap  for  the onshore pipeline during project execution stage.
- The specialized independent third party shall be subject to the approval of the Owner
- Proper marking on roadways for the movement of heavy equipment on FRP pipeline routing.
- Where applicable, thrust blocks, which are concrete pipe thrust restraints or anchors placed up against underground pipe fittings, should be used to prevent movement of underground pipes from thrust forces in water mains.
- Also, and where applicable, permanent markers for underground utilities like cable duct banks, direct buried cables, pipes etc. shall be specified.
- When encasing FRP lines in concrete, we should use a Neoprene pad to protect the pipe, or if the pipe crosses a road, we could install it within a trench or sleeve, which is a good solution because there will be no weight transfer to the pipe. The bottom line is that the concrete must not come into direct contact with the FRP pipe.
- In addition to the above requirements, the Document Management system for the Fibre Glass Pipeline, shall  be  included  as  Schedule  R  of  this  Specification  and  shall  be  followed  by  the  Contractor.  This management system shall include the requirement of Design, material selection, supplying, trenching, laying, jointing, workmanship, testing of Fiberglass pipeline to be followed by the EPC Contractor.
